Authors: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70648
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43069728



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is central to cervical lesion development, but single viral-load measurements may not capture heterogeneous viral dynamics. This study characterized longitudinal viral-load trajectories among women with persistent infection and evaluated their associations with cervical lesions and incremental predictive value beyond baseline factors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort of 1502 HPV-positive women followed at approximately 6-month intervals, latent class growth analysis using actual follow-up time was conducted among 624 women with type-specific persistent infection. Associations between trajectory group and any cervical lesion (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion [HSIL]) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression; HSIL was explored using Firth-penalized regression. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were used to assess incremental predictive performance. RESULTS: Of 1170 women with classifiable outcomes, 624 had persistent infection. Four trajectories were identified: low stable (39.6%), moderate declining (18.9%), moderate increasing (29.8%), and persistently high (11.7%). Any-lesion prevalence was 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4%, respectively (p < .001). Compared with the low-stable group, fully adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.95 (95% CI, 1.02-3.74), 29.66 (95% CI, 16.75-52.51), and 124.29 (95% CI, 47.30-326.60) for the other groups, respectively. The persistently high group was also associated with HSIL (OR, 9.47; 95% CI, 3.18-33.09). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) increased from 0.713 for the base model to 0.888 for both the simple longitudinal and trajectory models and 0.899 for the joint model. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal HPV viral-load dynamics identified clinically distinct risk phenotypes. Moderate-increasing and persistently high trajectories were strongly associated with cervical lesions, whereas longitudinal information improved discrimination beyond baseline measurements. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

Authors: Petrelli F, Meregalli G, Berzi D, Nicolì F, Viglino F, Della Pepa G, Indovina F, Dalmiglio C, Forloni F, Bossi A, et al.
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103273
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43063527



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria. FINDINGS: We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was largely attributable to comparator restriction, choice of estimator, and handling of zero-event trials rather than to differences in cancer ascertainment. Observational syntheses suggested lower hepatocellular carcinoma risk (hazard ratio 0·60, 95% CI 0·41-0·88), but four reviews had very high overlap (CCA 50·0%). Outcome-level certainty was moderate for five outcomes, low for 11, and very low for five; none was high. No association met class I or II credibility criteria. INTERPRETATION: Randomised evidence shows no evidence of a material increase in overall or site-specific cancer risk over currently observed trial durations (median about 70 weeks, maximum about 5 years), and cancer concerns alone do not justify withholding indicated GLP-1RA treatment. Small, rare, long-latency, dose-specific, or agent-specific effects cannot be excluded, and the evidence cannot address exposure beyond approximately five years, well short of the 8-10 years generally required to evaluate cancer incidence. Observational protective associations should not support causal or cancer-prevention claims. FUNDING: None.

Authors: Letizia F, Emanuele V, Pietro O, Alberto M, Matteo A, Elena MM, Alessandra I, Ida F, Alessandra V, Andrea M, et al.
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71073
Published: 2026-Nov-27
PMID: 43100145



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To evaluate the real-world effectiveness of mepolizumab on sinonasal symptoms, endoscopic disease severity, olfactory function, and OCS use in patients with EGPA and CRSwNP, and to explore potential predictors of sinonasal response. METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center study including 21 adult patients with EGPA-associated CRSwNP treated with mepolizumab 300 mg every 4 weeks for at least 12 months. All patients received intranasal mometasone furoate; concomitant OCS and immunosuppressive therapy were allowed. Sinonasal outcomes were assessed at baseline and follow-up using SNOT-22, NPS, and Sniffin' Sticks Identification Test-16 (SSIT-16). Blood eosinophil count (BEC), OCS use, and potential predictors of response were also analyzed. RESULTS: After 12 months, mepolizumab significantly reduced BEC from 940 to 60 cells/μL (p < 0.00001), improved SNOT-22 from 55 to 21.5 (p < 0.0005) and NPS from 5 to 2 (p < 0.005), and increased SSIT-16 from 6 to 11 (p < 0.005). SNOT-22 improved significantly at 6 months, with further improvement at 12 months. At 12 months, 76.2% of patients achieved the SNOT-22 MCID, 85.7% reached good symptom control, and 42.9% became normosmic; anosmia decreased from 76.2% to 38.1%. OCS use declined from 80.9% to 28.6%, with a median dose reduction from 5 mg to 0. ANCA positivity and a higher number of previous sinus surgeries were associated with poorer sinonasal response. CONCLUSION: In this real-world EGPA cohort, mepolizumab significantly improved sinonasal quality of life, endoscopic polyp burden, olfactory function, and OCS dependence over 12 months. These findings support IL-5 blockade as an effective therapeutic option for sinonasal manifestations of EGPA-associated CRSwNP.

Authors: Liu J, Cheng X, Geng Y, Cao P, Zou P, Wang Y, Luan Q
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70567
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43099907



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite growing evidence of the involvement of mitochondria in inflammation, the roles of specific mtDNA outside the mitochondria in periodontitis have been little explored. To address this knowledge gap, we explore the effects and mechanisms of mtDNA efflux in the development of periodontitis. METHODS: First, we identified the potential of HGFs as a "non-classical" component of the immune system in response to bacteria and damage-related signals using single-cell analysis. Next, we detected mtDNA efflux in HGFs and gingiva during periodontitis using immunofluorescence, adenovirus transduction, and real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. In addition, we investigated the role of free mtDNA in periodontitis and its associated mechanisms. RESULTS: We confirmed the "immune role" of HGFs. Furthermore, lipopolysaccharide induced the upregulation of reactive oxygen species in HGFs enabling mtDNA efflux, which significantly promoted the expression and secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines in HGFs. MtDNA efflux drives alveolar bone loss in wild-type and periodontitis mice. Mechanistically, the involvement in periodontitis of mtDNA efflux was associated with the upregulation of the cGAS-STING-NF-κB pathway. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the effect of mtDNA efflux on the activation of periodontitis. Future studies focusing on the ablation of mtDNA efflux in HGFs may lead to promising treatment responses for periodontitis.

Authors: Vasudevan SS, Latour M, Ahmed OG, Yim MT
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71085
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43099239



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify oncologic, orbital, and ocular outcomes after orbital preservation (OP) and orbital exenteration (OE) in advanced sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC) invading the orbit. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched from inception through September 2026; reporting followed the PRISMA 2020 statement. Studies of at least 10 patients with SNSCC involving the orbit that reported survival, recurrence, or orbital outcomes by orbital management were included. Proportions were pooled separately within OP and OE arms using random-effects models, and cohorts reporting both arms were pooled as odds ratios. RESULTS: Of 794 records, 20 studies with 1111 patients were included (reported mean or median age, 53-67 years; 67.3% male). Pooled 5-year overall survival was 63.4% (95% CI, 48.1-77.6) after OP and 65.3% (95% CI, 38.1-88.6; 73 patients) after OE (p = 0.92). Local recurrence (27.3% vs. 30.8%; p = 0.57) and 5-year disease-free survival (52.1% vs. 48.2%; p = 0.71) also did not differ. The orbit was preserved in 79.3% (95% CI, 67.3-89.3), ranging from 69.1% with surgery to 98.1% with definitive chemoradiotherapy (p < 0.001). Among preserved orbits, 85.9% retained a functional eye and 2.0% required delayed exenteration. In 6 cohorts reporting both arms, the odds of 5-year survival did not differ (odds ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.38-2.25). CONCLUSION: OP was not associated with inferior survival, disease-free survival, or local control compared with OE, and roughly 4 of 5 orbits were retained, most functional. Sparse OE data and wide confidence intervals preclude conclusions of equivalence.

Authors: Luo X, Zhao H, Wang X, Liu K, Shang Z
Journal: Oncogene | DOI: 10.1038/s41388-026-04050-x
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43099150



Abstract:
Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are abundant in the tumor microenvironment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and exert pivotal pro-tumorigenic functions, including extracellular matrix remodeling, angiogenesis, and immunosuppression. In this study, we investigated the molecular mechanisms by which CAFs orchestrate the recruitment and functional polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) to drive HNSCC progression. Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), a key regulator of CAFs, exhibited a markedly positive correlation with CD163+ macrophage infiltration in human HNSCC tissues. Functional validation demonstrated that NNMT mediated CAF-driven recruitment and M2 polarization of TAMs in HNSCC in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, NNMT upregulated CCL2 secretion in CAFs, facilitating CCR2-dependent TAM recruitment and M2 polarization in HNSCC. Moreover, NNMT activated the PI3K/Akt pathway, leading to upregulation of the EBF transcription factor 1 (EBF1), which directly regulates CCL2 transcription in CAFs. Furthermore, the combination of NNMT inhibitors and anti-PD-1 antibodies synergistically suppressed tumor growth and modulated anti-tumor immunity in a syngeneic mouse model. In conclusion, these findings reveal that the NNMT/PI3K/Akt/EBF1 signaling axis contributes to CAF-mediated TAM recruitment and M2 polarization in HNSCC through the CCL2/CCR2 axis. Our study sheds new light on CAF-macrophage crosstalk in HNSCC and provides potential therapeutic strategies for patients.

Authors: Qin S, Ma J, Zhang Y, Li H, Mao Y, Yang W, Xie Z, Liu Y, Wan L, Zhang X, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00456-0
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43098165



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia can disrupt planned chemotherapy through treatment delay, dose reduction, discontinuation, or rescue therapy. We assessed the efficacy and safety of rafutrombopag, an oral thrombopoietin receptor agonist, in patients with solid tumours and established chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia associated with platinum-based chemotherapy. METHODS: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial done at 43 sites in China, adults aged 18-75 years with solid tumours, platelet count less than 75 × 109/L, and an actual thrombocytopenia-related chemotherapy delay of at least 7 days associated with platinum-based combination chemotherapy were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to continuous rafutrombopag, switch rafutrombopag, or placebo. During the pre-chemotherapy correction period, patients in the continuous and switch groups received 7·5 mg oral rafutrombopag once daily and patients in the placebo group received matching placebo during the correction period; patients in the switch group changed to placebo when cycle 1 chemotherapy began. The protocol target for resuming chemotherapy was a platelet count of at least 100 × 109/L. Response was assessed within 14 days; patients who had not responded by day 14 could receive rescue therapy, resume chemotherapy, or both at the investigator's discretion. During two subsequent 3-week chemotherapy cycles, the continuous group continued platelet-guided rafutrombopag (2·5 mg dose-level adjustments; maximum 15 mg once daily), and the switch and placebo groups received matching placebo. The primary endpoint was a composite response, defined as platelet response (platelet count of at least 100 × 109/L) within 14 days after starting study treatment, completion of the first on-study chemotherapy cycle using the same chemotherapy regimen as before enrolment, platelet count of at least 75 × 109/L on cycle 1 day 21, and no platelet-increasing rescue therapy before cycle 1 day 21. Efficacy was analysed in the intention-to-treat population and safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05864014) and is complete. FINDINGS: Between April 27, 2023, and March 3, 2025, 213 patients were randomly assigned to continuous rafutrombopag (n=70), switch rafutrombopag (n=72), or placebo (n=71). Overall, 211 (99%) patients entered the pre-chemotherapy correction period and received at least one dose of study treatment. The median age of enrolled patients was 61 years (IQR 56-68), 112 (53%) were male and 101 (47%) were female. 204 (96%) of 213 patients were Han Chinese and nine (4%) were from other ethnic groups. The primary endpoint was met by 53 (76%) of 70 patients in the continuous group, 35 (49%) of 72 in the switch group, and 28 (39%) of 71 in the placebo group. Compared with placebo, the absolute difference was 36·2 percentage points (95% CI 21·0 to 51·3; p<0·0001) for continuous rafutrombopag and 9·0 percentage points (-7·2 to 25·1; p=0·28) for switch rafutrombopag. In the safety set, adverse events occurred in 63 (90%) of 70 patients in the continuous group, 65 (92%) of 71 in the switch group, and 65 (93%) of 70 in the placebo group. Grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 18 (26%), 26 (37%), and 22 (31%) patients, and serious adverse events in five (7%), eight (11%), and ten (14%), respectively. The most common adverse events were white blood cell count decreased (36 [51%], 38 [54%], and 44 [63%]), neutrophil count decreased (32 [46%], 44 [62%], and 44 [63%]), and anaemia (20 [29%], 25 [35%], and 16 [23%]) in the continuous, switch, and placebo groups, respectively. Liver enzyme-related adverse events occurred in 16 (23%), 13 (18%), and 18 (26%) patients. No fatal adverse events occurred during the double-blind treatment phase. INTERPRETATION: In patients with solid tumours and established chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia associated with platinum-based chemotherapy with an actual thrombocytopenia-related chemotherapy delay, continuous rafutrombopag improved the prespecified composite primary endpoint compared with placebo. The switch regimen did not show a significant difference from placebo. Safety findings should be interpreted in the context of cancer and ongoing chemotherapy. FUNDING: Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals.

Authors: Blauvelt A, Armstrong AW, Ehst BD, Gold LFS, Sofen H, Tyring SK, Soung J, Papp KA, Bhatia N, Alam MS, et al.
Journal: Lancet (London, England) | DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01649-1
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43098154



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Safe and highly effective oral treatment options for patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis are scarce. Here, we aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of envudeucitinib (ESK-001), an investigational next-generation, highly selective, oral, allosteric tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor, in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: ONWARD1 (NCT06586112) and ONWARD2 (NCT06588738) are completed, replicate, multicentre, randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled and active comparator-controlled, phase 3 trials that enrolled patients in 333 sites (eg, research and medical centres, private practices, and hospitals) across 19 countries. Adults with a diagnosis of plaque psoriasis for at least 6 months, body surface area of at least 10%, and Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) of at least 12 were randomly assigned 2:1:1 to oral envudeucitinib 40 mg twice daily, placebo, or apremilast 30 mg twice daily for 24 weeks of treatment. At week 16, patients receiving placebo were transitioned to envudeucitinib. Coprimary endpoints were at least 75% improvement from baseline in Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI 75) and static Physician's Global Assessment (sPGA) of 0 or 1 at week 16 (envudeucitinib vs placebo). Secondary endpoints were assessed at weeks 16 and 24 (envudeucitinib vs placebo and/or apremilast). Safety assessments included adverse events and laboratory parameters. FINDINGS: From July 25, 2024, to Dec 18, 2025, 912 and 859 patients were randomly assigned to ONWARD1 and ONWARD2, respectively (envudeucitinib, n=459 and n=433; placebo, n=230 and n=211; apremilast, n=223 and n=215). In both trials, coprimary and all key secondary endpoints were met (all p<0·0001). At week 16, envudeucitinib resulted in statistically significant PASI 75 responses versus placebo (ONWARD1: 351 [76·5%] of 459 vs 43 [18·7%] of 230; ONWARD2: 305 [70·4%] of 433 vs 29 [13·7%] of 211; both p<0·0001) and sPGA of 0 or 1 responses versus placebo (ONWARD1: 280 [61·0%] of 459 vs 23 [10·0%] of 230; ONWARD2: 248 [57·3%] of 433 vs 12 [5·7%] of 211; both p<0·0001). Up to week 16, 525 (59·0%) of 890 receiving envudeucitinib, 166 (37·6%) of 441 receiving placebo, and 224 (51·1%) of 438 patients receiving apremilast had one or more treatment-emergent adverse event. Up to week 24, 566 (63·6%) of 890 and 248 (56·6%) of 438 patients originally randomly assigned to envudeucitinib or apremilast had one or more treatment-emergent adverse event. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mostly mild or moderate and responsive to standard therapies; headache (97 [10·9%] of 890), nasopharyngitis (93 [10·4%] of 890), acne (60 [6·7%] of 890), and upper respiratory tract infection (57 [6·4%] of 890) occurred in at least 5% of patients receiving envudeucitinib during the trials. Up to week 16, serious adverse events occurred in 19 (2·1%) of 890 patients receiving envudeucitinib, five (1·1%) of 441 patients receiving placebo, and five (1·1%) of 438 patients receiving apremilast. INTERPRETATION: Envudeucitinib improved both skin signs and patient-reported outcomes, and maintained favourable tolerability, supporting its role as a promising oral treatment for patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. FUNDING: Alumis.

Authors: Benaran I, Bhardwaj S, Lim AE, Montgomery J, Milner T
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108241
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43097977



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) has comparable oncological outcomes and the potential to improve functional outcomes in comparison to radiotherapy in early HPV positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), and improved functional outcomes in comparison to open surgery. However there is limited data in the HPV negative population. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review aims to assess the existing data on TORS outcomes in the treatment of HPV negative OPSCC. EVIDENCE REVIEW: Following the PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted using Medline, Embase, Pubmed, Cinahl, Cochrane Libraries, Prospero and Web of Science between 2010-2026. Articles reporting outcomes of HPV negative OPSCC managed using TORS were included. FINDINGS: A total of 10 studies of patients undergoing TORS for HPV negative OPSCC were included with 1 study being prospective. Oncological survival outcomes and functional outcomes were assessed. 2-year overall survival rate (OSR) ranged from 81 to 95 % and 5-year OSR from 65.9 to 92.4 %. Rates of reported long term gastrostomy tube dependence ranged from 1.8 to 5.4 %.Tracheostomy rates ranged from 10.5 % to 35.7 %, of which 100 % were decannulated leaving no long term tracheostomies. Return to theatre rate for haemorrhage was between 1.8 % and 3.6 %. The mean length of hospital stay ranged from 3-5.8 days overall. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: This review demonstrates encouraging oncological outcomes following TORS, for HPV negative OPSCC, particularly for early-stage disease. Perioperative and long-term functional outcomes are also favourable, highlighting that TORS is a promising treatment modality which may be considered in selected patients.
